tier1.text: Each occipital lobe works mainly on vision: seeing, recognizing and identifying the world we see. It sits at the back of the brain. It is a region of the cerebral cortex, the folded outer layer of the brain. Signals from the eyes reach its primary visual cortex, where basic shapes start to be recognized.

quotes.quote: The outermost part of the brain is a thick piece of nervous system tissue called the cerebral cortex, which is folded into hills called gyri (singular: gyrus) and valleys called sulci (singular: sulcus).
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: For example, the visual pathway projects from the retinae through the thalamus to the primary visual cortex in the occipital lobe. This area is primarily in the medial wall within the longitudinal fissure. Here, visual stimuli begin to be recognized as basic shapes.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
